```{r}
library(dada2); packageVersion("dada2")
library(decontam)
library(ggplot2)
library(phyloseq)
library(openxlsx)
library(Biostrings)
library(dplyr)
library(microbiome)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(ggpubr)
library(vegan)
path <- "/home///18s.read/"
list.files(path)
```


```{r}
# Forward and reverse fastq filenames have format: SAMPLENAME_R1_001.fastq and SAMPLENAME_R2_001.fastq
fnFs <- sort(list.files(path, pattern="_R1_001.fastq", full.names = TRUE))
fnRs <- sort(list.files(path, pattern="_R2_001.fastq", full.names = TRUE))
# Extract sample names, assuming filenames have format: SAMPLENAME_XXX.fastq
sample.names <- sapply(strsplit(basename(fnFs), "_"), `[`, 1)
plotQualityProfile(fnFs[1:59])
plotQualityProfile(fnRs[1:59])
```

```{r}
# Place filtered files in filtered/ subdirectory
filtFs <- file.path(path, "filtered", paste0(sample.names, "_F_filt.fastq.gz"))
filtRs <- file.path(path, "filtered", paste0(sample.names, "_R_filt.fastq.gz"))
names(filtFs) <- sample.names
names(filtRs) <- sample.names
out <- filterAndTrim(fnFs, filtFs, fnRs, filtRs, trimLeft=c(19,20), truncLen=c(240,160),
                     maxN=0, maxEE=c(2,2), truncQ=2, rm.phix=TRUE,
                     compress=TRUE, multithread=TRUE) 
head(out)
```
#Learn errors forward
```{r}
errF <- learnErrors(filtFs, multithread=TRUE)
```
#lear errors reverse
```{r}
errR <- learnErrors(filtRs, multithread=TRUE)
```
#subset
```{r}
plotErrors(errF, nominalQ=TRUE)
dadaFs <- dada(filtFs, err=errF, multithread=TRUE)
dadaRs <- dada(filtRs, err=errR, multithread=TRUE)
dadaFs[[1]]
mergers <- mergePairs(dadaFs, filtFs, dadaRs, filtRs, verbose=TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Inspect the merger data.frame from the first sample
head(mergers[[1]])
seqtaball <- makeSequenceTable(mergers)
dim(seqtaball)
table(nchar(getSequences(seqtaball)))
seqtab <- seqtaball[,nchar(colnames(seqtaball)) %in% 240:387]
seqtab.nochim <- removeBimeraDenovo(seqtab, method="consensus", multithread=TRUE, verbose=TRUE)
dim(seqtab.nochim)
sum(seqtab.nochim)/sum(seqtab)
getN <- function(x) sum(getUniques(x))
track <- cbind(out, sapply(dadaFs, getN), sapply(dadaRs, getN), sapply(mergers, getN), rowSums(seqtab.nochim))

```

```{r}
# save sequences with original headers
write.csv(t(seqtab.nochim), paste0("seqtab-nochim.csv"), quote=FALSE)


# simplify names to sequence headers(seq1, seq2...seq100...)
seqs <- colnames(seqtab.nochim)
SeqName <- vector(dim(seqtab.nochim)[2], mode="character")
SeqName_ft <- vector(dim(seqtab.nochim)[2], mode="character")
for (i in 1:dim(seqtab.nochim)[2]) {
  SeqName[i] <- paste("seq", i, sep="")
  SeqName_ft[i] <- paste(">seq", i, sep="")
}

# write sequences in a FASTA file
fastaseqs_ft <- rbind(SeqName_ft, seqs)
write(fastaseqs_ft, paste0("fastaseqs.fasta"))


# write sequences in a FASTA file (tabular)
fastaseqs <- cbind(SeqName, seqs)
write.csv(fastaseqs, paste0("fastaseqs.csv"), quote=FALSE, row.names = FALSE)


# write count table
seqtab.nochim.t <- t(seqtab.nochim)
row.names(seqtab.nochim.t) <- SeqName
seqtab.nochim.t <- tibble::rownames_to_column(as.data.frame(seqtab.nochim.t), "SeqName")
write.csv(seqtab.nochim.t, paste0("counts.csv"), quote=FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

# write taxonomy table
taxtable <- taxa.PR
row.names(taxtable) <- SeqName
taxtable <- tibble::rownames_to_column(as.data.frame(taxtable), "SeqName")
write.csv(taxtable, paste0("taxtable.csv"), quote=FALSE, row.names = FALSE)


# Join results and save in spreadsheet (excel) format

tax_counts <- left_join(taxtable, seqtab.nochim.t, by = "SeqName", keep = TRUE)
tax_counts_fasta <- left_join(tax_counts, as.data.frame(fastaseqs), by = c("SeqName.x" = "SeqName"), keep = TRUE)
openxlsx::write.xlsx(tax_counts_fasta, file = paste0("18s.reads_ASV_PR2.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE, asTable = FALSE, sheetName = "18s.reads", firstRow = TRUE, zoom = 90, keepNA = TRUE)
```

#The vector for decontam is avector that distinguishes blanks (TRUE) from samples (FALSE). This chunk is creating a decontaminated taxonomy table and count table with an algortithm that sorts out taxa deemed as contaminants.
```{r}

vector_for_decontam<- as.logical(c("TRUE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "TRUE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "TRUE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "TRUE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "TRUE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE", "FALSE"
))
contam_df <- isContaminant(t(asv_tab), neg=vector_for_decontam)
table(contam_df$contaminant)
contam_asvs <- row.names(contam_df[contam_df$contaminant == TRUE, ])

contam_indices <- which(asv_fasta %in% paste0(">", contam_asvs))
dont_want <- sort(c(contam_indices, contam_indices + 1))
asv_fasta_no_contam <- asv_fasta[- dont_want]

asv_tax[row.names(asv_tax) %in% contam_asvs, ]
asv_tab_no_contam <- asv_tab[!row.names(asv_tab) %in% contam_asvs, ]
asv_tax_no_contam <- asv_tax[!row.names(asv_tax) %in% contam_asvs, ]

write(asv_fasta_no_contam, "18ASVs-no-contam.fa")
write.table(asv_tab_no_contam, "18ASVs_counts-no-contam.tsv",
            sep="\t", quote=F, col.names=NA)
write.table(asv_tax_no_contam, "18ASVs_taxonomy-no-contam.tsv",
            sep="\t", quote=F, col.names=NA)



```

#we want to aggregate our taxa to a level, in this case i've chosen "family" but you can change this area of the code to "class", "order", "genus" etc. Then first we use the transform() to make the data "compositional", which transforms it into relative abundance.
```{r}
# Aggregate at seperate level (note that our trainer.fasta has options: SeqName / Domain / Supergroup / Division / Subdivision / Class / Order / Family / Genus / Species / OTU)
YEL.rel <- aggregate_taxa(YEL.asv.com, "Genus")
YEL.Fam <- aggregate_taxa(YEL.asv.com, "Family")
YEL.Order <- aggregate_taxa(YEL.asv.com, "Order")

# Transform to relative abundance
YEL.Genus <- microbiome::transform(YEL.rel, "compositional")
rel.Fam <- microbiome::transform(YEL.Fam, "compositional")
rel.Order <- microbiome::transform(YEL.Order, "compositional")

```

#phyloseq's top_taxa(data, n=x) creates a vector, and then we can subset the taxa in the original phyloseq object using prune_taxa() and te vector we just ceated. This way we can plot only the most abundant Taxa for analysis.
```{r}
#get the nams of the top 13 most abundant taxa
TTN <- top_taxa(YEL.Genus, n=13)
TTN.F <- top_taxa(rel.Fam, n=13)
TTN.O <- top_taxa(rel.Order, n=13)

#Remove NAs if present, all had "unknown" as [1]. if it was [6] we'd ammend the code to show data[-6]
#TTN.G <- TTN[-1]
#TTN.FA <-TTN.F[-1]
#TTN.OR <- TTN.O[-1]
#you may not need this code with the filter taxic lines below


# Subset the taxa in the original objects
Pruned_18s_Gen <- prune_taxa(TTN, YEL.Genus)
Pruned_18s_Fam <- prune_taxa(TTN.F, rel.Fam)
Pruned_18s_Ord <- prune_taxa(TTN.O, rel.Order)


# Filter taxic object to remove rows with NA in Genus
#Everytime you run this line is will flip the results in the plot, meaning if NAs are present, you must go back and run this line.
taxic_filtered <- taxic[!is.na(taxic$Genus), ]
taxic_filtered <- taxic[!is.na(taxic$Family), ]
taxic_filtered <- taxic[!is.na(taxic$Order), ]



```

#we need to perform rarefaction on our data to normalize for diversity analysis. It is ultimately the choise of a researcher on whether they want to aggreate the data to a taxa level. I have decided not to do this, but  specific resolution diversity metrics can be created with simply a single line of code if desire.
```{r}
# Load the required packages
library(ggpubr)

# Assuming 'MetaData' is your metadata dataframe
sample_names <- rownames(MetaDataB)

# Generate a vector of colors with unique colors for each sample name
sample_colors <- rainbow(45)

# Create a dataframe with 'sample_names' as the row names and 'sample_colors' as a column named 'Color'
sample_colors_df <- data.frame(SampleName = sample_names, Color = sample_colors, row.names = sample_names)

# Create the rarefaction curve plot and convert it to a ggplot2 object
rarecurve_plot <- rarecurve(t(count_table_filtered), step = 100, col = sample_colors_df$Color, lwd = 2, ylab = "ASVs", label = FALSE)
abline(v = min(rowSums(t(count_table_filtered))))

# Add the legend with smaller text and multiple columns using the 'legend' function
legend("topright", legend = sample_colors_df$SampleName, fill = sample_colors_df$Color, title = "Sample Names", cex = 0.4, ncol = 2)

# Add the centered title to the plot
title("18s rarefaction curves", cex.main = 1.5)
```

#Now we will Plot 18s Bray-Curtis distances. To do so we need to aggreagte our rarefied_phyloseq to A taxa level, i've decided Genus, Then tranfsorm it to compositional, we don't necessaerily need to subset the data to only show the top taxa becasue we want to find natural trends. 
```{r}

#the following chunk assumes all all prior packages (phyloseq, microbiome, etc) have been loaded
#the vegan package is the only new one

library(vegan)

load("/home/spanuser3/Documents/my_workspace_B.RData")

#aggregate to genus level
rarefied_genus <- aggregate_taxa(rarefied_physeq, "Genus")

# Transform to relative abundance
rarefied_genus <- microbiome::transform(rarefied_genus, "compositional")

#rarefied_genus@phy_tree <- NULL 

# Assuming "Site" is a character column and "Date" is a character/numeric column in the metadata (Phy.meta)
# If needed, convert "Site" and "Date" to factors for better plotting
sample_data(rarefied_genus)$Site <- factor(sample_data(rarefied_genus)$Site)
sample_data(rarefied_genus)$Date <- factor(sample_data(rarefied_genus)$Date)

# Calculate Bray-Curtis dissimilarity matrix
bray_curtis_dist <- phyloseq::distance(rarefied_genus, method = "bray")

# Perform PCA using the Bray-Curtis dissimilarity matrix
pca_result <- cmdscale(bray_curtis_dist, k = 2, eig = TRUE)

# Extract PCA scores for plotting
pca_scores <- as.data.frame(pca_result$points)

# Add Site and Date information to the PCA scores data frame
pca_scores$Site <- sample_data(rarefied_genus)$Site
pca_scores$Date <- sample_data(rarefied_genus)$Date

# Create a 2D PCA plot
p <- ggplot(pca_scores, aes(x = V1, y = V2, color = Site)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(title = "18s Bray-Curtis PCA ", x = "PC1", y = "PC2") +
  theme_minimal()

# Facet the plot by Date (assuming Date is a character or factor column)
p_faceted <- p + facet_wrap(~ Date)

# Print the faceted plot
print(p_faceted)

pdf_file <- "/home/spanuser3/Documents/18s_braycurtis_PCA"
ggsave(filename = pdf_file, plot = p_faceted, device = "pdf")
```


#This plot has visualized the bray-curtis distance measurements by treatment site during each sampling month. There are many different ways to plot this, but I thought this was a good start. 
```{r}
# Assuming you have already run the previous code to create 'pca_scores' data frame

# Assuming you have already run the previous code to create 'pca_scores' data frame

# Load the necessary library if not already loaded
library(ggplot2)

# Plot the data with ggplot
byplot <- ggplot(pca_scores, aes(x = V1, y = V2, color = Site, shape = Date)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  labs(x = "PC1", y = "PC2") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(15, 25, 16, 18, 17)) + # Specify different shapes for each month
  scale_color_discrete(name = "Site") + # Specify the legend title for color
  ggtitle("18s Bray Curtis PCA") + # Add the plot title
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) # Center the plot title
```
